argument_summary: The certification claim should be narrowed, not treated as a clean showing that rollout controls resolved the issue. The admissible record supports that aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the launch posture is monitored and reversible at 6%. The same record also shows the utility arrears assistance segment remains exposed, the rollout gate does not exclude it, and there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. On that evidence, the strongest supportable position is certification only in a caveated form: the limitation must be treated as an unresolved, explicitly disclosed model-card limitation, while rollout controls operate as monitoring and containment rather than as a substitute for the policy predicate.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not offered as a substitute for policy compliance. The only operational point supported by the admissible record is that the 6% monitored rollout with rollback limits blast radius while the unresolved limitation is carried forward transparently; that risk-weighted posture supports avoiding unnecessary escalation if the auditor records the certification as caveated rather than fully clean.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not permit treating a rollback switch, dashboarding, or a small initial percentage as curing disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed. That part of the audit concern is correct. The overbroad part is any implication that the packet therefore supports nothing at all. The admissible evidence still supports a narrower position: rollout and monitoring are relevant deployment mitigations, aggregate readiness and rehearsal results are relevant launch-readiness facts, and the certification decision is defensible only as caveated compliance tied to explicit acknowledgment of the unresolved limitation rather than as clean compliance from rollout controls alone.
concessions: The affected utility arrears assistance segment remains below target on payment-plan eligibility explanation and is included in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate does not exclude the affected use case.
The current risk acceptance draft is not approved and does not address utility arrears assistance exposure.
The present record does not support any claim that monitored rollout plus rollback, by itself, satisfies the disclosure policy.
The present record does not prove clean compliance if the question is whether the weakness was already resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
private_or_side_channel_content: No private or side-channel material is offered as support. No new evidence is added.
